Thanks Rishi —

Confirming the list you captured is accurate. A couple specifics from our side: 
- Required PII in prompts: patient name, MRN, DOB, limited contact info; occasionally short clinical notes (no attachments).
- Retention: HealthSys policy is that PII-containing prompts should not be retained persistently. Preference is that prompts are either not logged at all or retained for no more than 30 days for troubleshooting. Outputs that include PHI should be retained for no more than 30 days unless we explicitly opt in for longer retention.
- Residency: Must be US-only; primary region us-east-1.
- Encryption & keys: We require support for customer-managed KMS (or equivalent) for any stored data.
- Audit: Need API-level audit logs showing who accessed logs and when.

Please confirm what Redwood stores by default for hosted API (prompts, outputs, token-level logs, backups), what can be disabled, and what options we have on Dedicated/Private to meet our policy. Legal will send a DPA redline once we get your confirmation.

Hi Alex / Rishi / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. I’m copying the short answers here and attaching a one-page summary (redwood-pii-summary.pdf) for your legal team: 

What Redwood stores by default (hosted API):
- Request metadata (timestamp, model, route, token counts): retained by default for 365 days for billing/analytics.
- Full request prompts and model outputs: retained by default for 30 days, encrypted at rest. These logs are used for debugging, abuse detection, and model quality.
- Token-level tracing (temporarily used for debugging) is ephemeral and retained only for immediate troubleshooting (typically < 7 days) unless flagged.
- Backups / snapshots: encrypted, short-lived, and covered under retention policies; not used for analytics.

What we can change / options for HealthSys:
- Hosted: We can configure your tenant to disable persistent logging of prompts/outputs entirely (no stored plaintext prompts/outputs) — this will disable certain debugging features and some quality monitoring. You can still get aggregated metrics and billing.
- Dedicated: With Dedicated capacity we can disable prompt/output persistence by default and route all logs to your KMS-controlled storage (customer-managed KMS) inside the requested region.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Full control — no prompts/outputs are stored by Redwood unless you explicitly enable it.

Residency & encryption:
- We can pin your tenant to us-east-1 and ensure all encrypted storage and backups remain in-region.
- We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer BYOK (bring-your-own-key) on enterprise contracts and can discuss the required controls; otherwise we use AES-256 server-side encryption in the requested region.

Retention & access:
- Default prompts/outputs retention (hosted): 30 days. This is configurable downward to 0 days (effectively no persistent storage) for hosted tenants on enterprise plans. 
- Audit & access controls: we provide API-level audit logs and IAM controls; we can produce exportable audit logs for the period you require as part of the DPA.

Compliance artifacts: SOC 2 Type II report, encryption design doc, and a DPA template are available — I’ve attached redwood-pii-summary.pdf (one-page) for quick reference; we can provide the SOC2 pack under NDA.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi: confirm which deployment you prefer (Hosted with logging turned off, Dedicated, or Private) for the initial pilot.
2) Alex: legal sends redline to DPA-draft.docx.
3) Redwood (Neha + infra): schedule a 30-minute tech session to walk through KMS options and logging toggles.

If you want, I can produce a short statement that you can attach to your DPA redline that spells out: stored fields, storage location, retention window, and key controls — happy to produce that in a couple hours.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
